I have been farming this land for 30 years. My mother and my mother-in-law taught me most of what I know, and I watch what the neighbors do. Whatever works for them usually works for me.

My 8 mu — I split it like this: 5 mu I do wheat and corn together, one after the other on the same field. The other 3 mu I plant cotton. That is how I have always done it.

**Wheat** — I plant in October after the corn is off. I buy the same improved seed the seed shop in town sells, the kind my neighbor Auntie Liu always uses. She gets good wheat so I get the same. When I plant, I put down two big bags of compound fertilizer mixed into the soil — that is the base. Then in March when the wheat starts shooting up, I put a bag of urea on top. I water the wheat four times: once in November to protect it from the freeze, once in March when it grows fast, once when it flowers, and once when the grain is filling up. I spray for disease and weeds twice. I expect to get around 450 jin per mu — that is what I got last year.

**Corn** — Right after I cut the wheat in June, I rush to get the corn in. I use hybrid seed, everyone around here does. I put compound fertilizer down at planting and then when the corn is up to my waist I spread more urea. Corn eats a lot, you cannot be stingy. I water when I plant and once more in August if it does not rain. I spray for corn borer and sometimes for weeds. I expect about 550 jin per mu.

**Cotton** — Cotton is harder work. I plough that field in spring before planting in late April. Cotton needs more fertilizer spread across more times — base fertilizer at planting, then more when it starts setting bolls. I water three times. The bugs are the big worry — I spray four times through the season, mostly for aphids and bollworm. I expect about 250 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I will not cut corners on fertilizer. One year I tried using less and the wheat looked thin. It is not worth risking the harvest to save a bag.
